Short answer: pick an adjustable, integrated-LED task lamp with dimming and good lumen output (400–800 lm) — for example, the Harbor Task Lamp in your catalog is a good candidate. Below I explain why, what exact specs to look for, the evidence I have, and what still needs verification.

Why an integrated LED task lamp
- LEDs use far less power and last much longer than incandescent/halogen bulbs, so they give the biggest energy savings for desk lighting. Example estimate: a 10 W LED used 8 hours/day → ~29 kWh/year; a 60 W incandescent for the same use → ~175 kWh/year. That’s ~146 kWh saved per lamp per year (≈ $20–$30/yr at typical US residential rates). (This is a simple calculation — see “claims to verify” below.)
- Dimmable LEDs let you reduce wattage (and energy) while keeping the right light level for tasks.
- Adjustable arms and good optics let you light the work surface without glare or wasted light, increasing perceived brightness without higher power draw.
- Look for high efficacy (lm/W), appropriate lumen output, and an appropriate color temperature and CRI for your tasks.

Recommended target specs for an energy-efficient office desk lamp
- Light source: integrated LED (not incandescent/halogen)
- Power: typically 6–15 W for task lamps (depends on lumen output)
- Task output: 400–800 lumens for desk work (adjust as needed for large/small desks or very fine work)
- Efficacy: ideally >80 lm/W (higher is better)
- Color temperature: 3000–4000 K for a neutral/cool office feel (choose warmer if you prefer softer light)
- CRI: ≥80 for general offices; ≥90 if color accuracy matters
- Controls: dimming and (optional) color-temperature control
- Certifications/labels: ENERGY STAR or a Lighting Facts label where available
- Extras: articulated arm, swivel head, glare shield, and auto-off/occupancy sensor if you want additional savings

Evidence available from your catalog memory
- I found an entry called “Harbor Task Lamp” (and several generic “adjustable desk lamps” / “task lamps”) in your catalog memory. That indicates a task/desk lamp product is available in the catalog that matches the category you asked about.

Claims and product details that require verification
- I do not have detailed specs from the memory search (wattage, lumen output, efficacy, CRI, color-temperature range, dimming type, ENERGY STAR certification, sensor functionality, price, or warranty). Those are necessary to confirm that the Harbor Task Lamp (or any specific model) meets the energy-efficiency and performance targets above.
- The energy-savings example uses assumed wattages and a sample electricity price. Verify the lamp’s actual wattage, your expected daily hours, and local kWh price to compute the real savings.
- Confirm whether the lamp has integrated LEDs or replaceable bulbs, and whether it’s compatible with the type of dimmer you plan to use (some LEDs require specific dimmers).
- If you need documented certification (e.g., ENERGY STAR), confirm that the specific catalog item carries that certification.

Next steps I can take for you
- If you want, I can fetch the Harbor Task Lamp’s full specs (wattage, lumens, efficacy, CRI, CCT, dimming, ENERGY STAR, price, warranty) from your catalog memory and compare it to the target specs above.
- Or tell me your priorities (budget, style, need for color accuracy, desire for sensors/USB ports, desk size), and I’ll recommend 2–3 concrete models/choices and show the expected energy savings for each. Which would you prefer?
